messages:
jamie: heads up — Azure marketplace partner reported regressions after their recent driver/kernel upgrades. inference jobs falling back to CPU + occasional OOMs. can we triage driver/CUDA/ROCm pinning and a hotfix/rollback path? @alex @priya @vlad
alex: can you drop the partner logs here? short snippet or attach link is fine
jamie: pasted from partner's node:
```
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] model_server: allocation failed: requested 1835008000 bytes
GPU0: cuInit -> 0x1
cudart: kernel launch error: out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 212, in <module>
    infer_batch()
  File "serve.py", line 89, in infer_batch
    gpu.allocate(...)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```
jamie: partner says this started after switching to CUDA 12.2 + driver 535.x and mixing in ROCm nodes for hybrid clusters
vlad: hunch: kernel ABI mismatch + different cuBLAS/cuDNN builds. Recommend a small compatibility matrix: driver (535.86.*) + CUDA12.2 + cuDNN 9.1; and ROCm 5.4.x with matching ML libs. pin both image and host driver.
priya: agree. we need a shiproom-ready rollback playbook for marketplace images and an on-prem rollback for SI installs. also want a minimal repro that partner can run (single-batch, single-seq) so we don't chase unrelated drift
alex: i'll draft a compatibility matrix and a short repro script. will include specific package pins and kernel versions to request from partner. also will add a note about quant/INT8 kernels — those often blow memory if kernel mismatch
ops-bot: deploy-canary: marketplace-image-canary failed 2/3 tests — logs: https://redwood.internal/ci/2489/canary/123 (uploaded)
priya: ops: can you attach the failing test ids? we need them in the ticket for partner
ops-bot: attached tests: [infer-smoke-03, perf-reg-01] (see link above)
jamie: partner wants a quick hangout tomorrow. we should have the matrix + rollback ready before that. timeline: 09:00 PT canary run, 11:00 PT call with partner.
vlad: i'll prepare a small helm/daemonset patch that pins the node image + adds a node-exporter check for driver version. patch will be in draft PR by EOD
alex: matrix outline I'll publish in /docs/partners/compat-matrix.md and create a short checklist for marketplace listing (image pin, driver pin, kernel versions, repro steps).
priya: I'll loop in marketing for announcement freeze/statement. if this turns into an upstream driver hotfix we'll need joint messaging.
jamie: also flag legal/compliance? partner asked about CVEs in the driver. @priya can you note that for the call
priya: noted. I'll create the partner ticket and invite legal if CVE risk is mentioned on the call.
alex: quick ask — does anyone have a known-good combination we can suggest immediately? saves time on the call
vlad: from field testing: NVIDIA driver 535.101 + CUDA 12.2 + cuDNN 9.1 on Ubuntu 22.04 worked with our LLM suite. ROCm 5.4.2 on RHEL8 worked for AMD nodes. i'll include exact package hashes in the doc
jamie: perfect. action items:
- alex: publish compat matrix + repro script (link in thread)
- vlad: draft helm/rollback patch + node checks
- priya: partner ticket, ping marketing/legal, schedule call
- ops-bot: run marketplace canary at 09:00 PT tomorrow and report
please update thread when PRs/tickets/links exist :thumbsup:
alex: on it, will update before EOD
vlad: PR draft up: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4102 — includes pinning and healthcheck
priya: partner ticket created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/76221 — invited partner, legal on watch
ops-bot: scheduled: canary run queued for 2026-03-21T09:00:00-07:00
jamie: thanks everyone. we'll sync after the canary and before the partner call. trying to avoid a marketplace rollback but need clear rollback steps if canary fails
alex: will also add a short blurb for the marketplace listing about supported driver combinations so customers see it upfront
vlad: FYI i'll also add a note to the SI onboarding doc about kernel pinning and how to validate CUDA/cuDNN ABI compatibility
jamie: closing loop — update here with canary result and partner call minutes. :white_check_mark:
